question: Why does a COMPOUNDER_PASS analog leader warrant EXIT_IMMEDIATELY on existing shares and REJECTED on new capital at $263.75?

epigraph.quote: Admit the quality of the business, respect the verdict of the 200-day breakdown, and move 100% of at-risk capital back to cash.

web_blocks.html: Executive Thesis: Texas Instruments (NASDAQ: TXN) still earns a COMPOUNDER_PASS on business quality. It boasts a 300mm wafer cost moat, 22.04% ROIC, 64.2% Q3 gross margin, and 35% OBBBA tax credits.[2][12][27] Even so, Pass 1 checks and the November 20 selloff force a clear split between franchise quality and stock action. KPI health stays PASS_WITH_WATCH. Key risks include a 12% Analog buyer, ~50% physical China shipments (23% China HQ in Q3), and 194-day inventory ($4.67B). Balance-sheet watch items also include $15.65B pro-forma debt and Silicon Labs' $499M reverse break fee.[27][28][31][32][33]

Why EXIT_IMMEDIATELY (6.7226 Shares) & REJECTED (TIER_0) at $263.75: On November 20, TXN fell -7.70% to $263.75 on 16.82M shares (1.99x 20D / 2.49x Finviz average).[12][15] That drop broke the 50D SMA ($286.38), 30W SMA ($285.65), 200D SMA ($266.37), and 40W EMA ($264.22). The US market also sits in a 10-distribution-day Downtrend (38.8% > 50DMA; Semis Rank #21).[13][14][15] While facts_US tags Stage 1, snapshots_US enforces STAGE_4 (CAP_REJECTED). 4H RSI sits at 29.16 with NO_OPTIONS_EDGE.[13][16] Only $1.75 (0.12x ATR14) separates CMP from our prior $262.00 stop, creating gap risk. Meanwhile, $263.75 still prices in a 10.0% 10Y FCF CAGR post-Silicon Labs and just +6.07% expected value ($279.75) vs. 4.76%–5.04% Treasuries. We sell all 6.7226 Schwab shares ($1,773.09 value, -$226.88 loss) into 100% USD cash and rate new capital REJECTED (TREND, VALUATION).

book_paragraphs: Welcome to our refreshed institutional monograph on Texas Instruments Incorporated as of November 20, 2026. On business quality alone, Texas Instruments still earns an unambiguous COMPOUNDER_PASS. Its 80,000-product catalog, direct TI.com reach, 22.04% return on invested capital, 64.2% third-quarter gross margin, and 35% OBBBA Section 48D tax credits build a wide competitive moat.

Yet disciplined investing separates admiring a franchise from holding its shares through a broken tape. Over the past week, our Pass 1 forensic audit and the November 20 market breakdown converged on a stark warning. Fundamentally, we uncovered material concentration and balance-sheet watch items: a single unnamed Analog customer at 12% of sales, ~50% of 2025 shipments entering China, Silicon Labs' 30.9% China exposure paired with a $499 million reverse break fee, and $15.65 billion of pro-forma debt principal carrying a 101% Special Mandatory Redemption clause.

Technically, TXN closed Friday, November 20 at $263.75—down 7.70% on 16.82 million shares (nearly double average volume)—breaking below both its 50-day SMA ($286.38) and 200-day SMA ($266.37) inside a 10-distribution-day market Downtrend. While the quantitative facts ledger still mechanically reads Stage 1, the live snapshot classifies TXN as STAGE_4 (CAP_REJECTED), 4-hour RSI sits at 29.16 with no turn, and our Options Desk flags NO_OPTIONS_EDGE.

Consequently, both decisions are clear. For our held Schwab stake of 6.7226 shares ($1,999.97 cost basis, $1,773.09 value, 2.36% weight), we execute EXIT_IMMEDIATELY into 100% USD cash rather than risking a gap through our $262.00 prior stop. For new capital, even at $263.75 TXN still discounts a 10.0% ten-year FCF CAGR post-Silicon Labs and offers only +6.07% probability-weighted upside ($279.75 EV), so we assign REJECTED (TREND, VALUATION; TIER_0).

book_subsections.title: What Changed Since November 13 & What Must Happen to Re-Qualify
paragraphs: One week ago at $303.60, TXN sat above its 50-day and 200-day averages in a 6-distribution-day Correction, supporting a WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT posture with a $262.00 hard stop on our starter shares. By November 20, the U.S. market worsened into a 10-distribution-day Downtrend with only 38.8% of stocks above their 50-day averages, Semiconductor sector rank fell from #12 to #21, and TXN sliced through its 200-day SMA ($266.37) and 40-week EMA ($264.22) on 1.99x volume.

Because $263.75 sits just $1.75 (0.12x ATR14) above $262.00, holding for the final 66 basis points invites gap-down losses toward $248–$254. Moving 100% of the $1,773.09 proceeds into USD cash earning ~4.76% protects portfolio capital while keeping TXN on our long-term watchlist. We will only re-underwrite TXN for new capital after broad market breadth recovers above 50%, TXN completes a multi-week Stage 1 base near our conditional $225.00–$240.00 watch zone (or sub-$200 under a 10.5% CAPM WACC), and shares reclaim their 50-day moving average on institutional volume.

book_callouts.title: The One-Sentence Playbook
book_callouts.text: Exit all 6.7226 Schwab shares immediately at ~$263.75 into 100% USD cash, reject new capital on TREND and VALUATION (TIER_0), and revisit TXN only after a Stage 1 base and Stage 2 reclaim.
